Report Details

Violation ID: 8154887
Permit API: 051-23977
Unconventional: Yes
County: Fayette
Municipality: Washington Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/02/2023
Comments: On August 2 2023, the Department conducted a meeting with Diversified for the Brazzon 15 and Brazzon 7 stream crossing on site. Attending today's meeting included: Tyler Metzger (DEP ET), Jared Zinn (DEP), Samantha Kantorczy (DEP), Mike Stephan (DEP), Christy Owens (DEP), Scott Usher (Diversified), Charles Miller (Diversified), Samantha Foulk (DEP), Daniel Frick (Diversified), Jessica Nelko (Diversified), Rich Palya (Diversified), Heather Empfield (Diversified), Joe Vasinko (Markosky), and Ashley Brehm (Markosky).We met with Diversified representatives to discuss the path forward on the Brazzon 15 and 7 OG Wells emergency crossing situation.Diversified will notify the Department no later than Wednesday, August 9, 2023 if they decide to plug the gas well or proceed with pursuing a permanent access to the gas well. If Diversified decides to plug the gas well, they intend to access the gas well with a temporary access. If Diversified proceeds with plugging the gas well, they believe the plugging of the gas well can be completed within 6-8 months.Diversified indicated they have been trying to work with the landowners to access the gas well through their driveway, but the landowner does not want the Act 9 sign at the entrance of his driveway. Diversified stated they have legal rights to access through this driveway.A temporary GP-08 was reportedly submitted this morning that will be valid for approximately a year. It has not yet been reviewed and approved by the Department. The Emergency Permit currently approved expires on August 7, 2023.If Diversified pursued a permanent crossing at the stream, Technical Services notified Diversified that JPA would be needed.The Department inquired as to why the temporary crossing is not in. Diversified estimated that it would take 5-6 weeks for materials to be acquired and installed. Diversified stated that they will devise a plan and inform the Department. The Department has requested that Diversified remove debris from the culvert crossing on both sides of the stream bed that was previously installed.Diversified stated that all Act 9 signs with incorrect signage will be fixed. The Operator stated that the signs will be updated to ensure compliance with 78a55.Violations shall remain outstanding for the following:The Operator's ERP identifies an access road entrance that is not passable for emergency access vehicles and equipment. Therefore, the operator has failed to prepare and implement an ERP that provides for a proper response to emergencies that threaten human health and safety for the well site. As such, violations shall remain outstanding for the operators failure to prepare and implement an ERP that provides for a proper response to emergencies that threaten human health and safety for the well site.

Comments: On Friday February 1, 2019 I received notification of a produced water release at the NV72 CBM Well Site located in Morris Township, Washington County. On the same day, I spoke on the telephone with Mr. Kyle Borden from CNX Resources Partners (CNX) regarding details of the release and remediation efforts. On Monday February 4, 2019 I conducted a site inspection to further assess the situation. Following the inspection, I was contacted via telephone by Mr. Borden with an update to CNX's continued investigation which was completed prior to my inspection. There are five (5) production tanks connected in succession within a vegetated earthen berm containment structure which receives produced water from multiple gas wells in the area. The produced water enters tank 1 and will flow into each successive tank dependent upon the fluid level in the preceding tank. The fluid within the hose connecting tank 1 and tank 2 had become frozen during the recent polar vortex which impeded movement of fluid between the two tanks, thereby causing fluid from tank 1 to flow out of the top of the tank and into the containment structure. CNX estimated that approximately one (1) barrel of produced water flowed from the tank and into the berm structure which had ice coating the floor of the structure. The produced water had settled in a low spot within the berm structure near tank 1. The pooled water within the berm was vacuumed out of the berm with a vacuum truck. CNX arranged to have a vacuum truck return to the site to continue removing fluid from within the berm as the temperature continued to rise over the weekend and the ice within the berm melted. Representatives of CNX returned to the site on Monday morning, February 4, 2019, to continue their investigation and delineate any potential impact. Soil conductivity probe readings, ranging from less than one (1) mS/cm and not more than three (3) mS/cm were collected within the berm. Soil samples were collected from areas where the highest readings were observed for laboratory analysis to further determine impact. CNX will send the analytical results and a written summary of investigation activities to the Department for review upon receipt. During my Monday afternoon site inspection, soil conductivity readings were collected with a portable probe in accessible areas around tank 1 and tank 2. A part of the area was still covered in ice, ranging between one (1) and three (3) inches thick. Sections of the ground, not covered with ice, were observed to be frozen given the probe temperature readings and difficulty penetrating the earth with the probe. Readings around tank 1 ranged from less than one (1) mS/cm to just over one (1) mS/cm. Readings collected from the berm in front of tank 1 were less than one (1) mS/cm. The common value of two (2) to three (3) mS/cm used to remediate soils impacted by brine was not exceeded by readings collected by CNX and the Department. The release of fluid from the production tank and into the earthen berm structure surrounding the production tanks is a violation of 25 Pa. Code Section 78.54, 25 Pa. Code Section 78.57(a) and 35 P.S. Section 6018.301 (SWMA 301). The operator should respond in accordance with instructions in this notice.

Violation ID: 962592
Permit API: 123-42860
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Conewango Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/20/2022
Comments: On 07/20/2022, The Department received a call from Brian Haner, stating a tree had fallen on a the well overnight and had broken the gathering lines. There was crude getting into a unnamed tributary of Irvine run. An estimated 2+ barrels made its way off site. Upon arrival on site Mr. Haner had booms across the unnamed tributary in several locations. There was a small under flow dam built on a spring seep just below the well. There were also several booms placed at the mouth of the unnamed tributary to Irvine run. Oil absorbent pads were being used to collect oil behind the booms. The crude made its way from the well pad down to a spring seep approx 10-15 feet. The crude continued down the spring into an unnamed tributary of Irvine run approx 140 feet. The spill then continued down the unnamed tributary approx. 1/4 mile. There is some evidence of crude in Irvine run at this time but it is slight. Rain is predicted over the coming days. We spoke with Mr. Haner about placing some booms in a better suited areas. Rain is predicted and the unnamed tributary is prone rise very quickly with small amounts of precipitation. The unnamed trib channel is boulder strewn and very rocky. He said he would move the booms around and monitor them going forward. Mr. Haner also had a excavator in route. He was going to get the impacted soil nearest the well dug up and into containers. He was also going to better construct the underflow dam that was built in the spring flow area just below the well pad. The under flow that was built was functioning but with any appreciable amount of rain it may not handle the added flow.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 967895
Permit API: 015-23708
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Asylum Twp
Inspection Type: Drilling/Alteration
Inspection Date: 9/12/2022
Comments: On 9/12/2022, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Chesapeake Hopson well site. It was 68 degrees and overcast when I arrived on location. Measurable amounts of rainfall had impacted the region in the last 24 hours.I met Chesapeake's Justin Myers when I arrived at location. He said that drilling out the plugs on the nine new wells had been completed the day before. Crews were in the process of installing the production trees on the new wells plus the one existing well. Crews were in the process of removing the remaining equipment from the completions operations. The coil tubing unit left during the inspection. Two cranes were on site loading equipment onto trucks. Justin expects most of the equipment to be removed by tomorrow. The fresh water AST will be removed tomorrow and he expects the crews to start removing the rig matting and secondary containment. Justin accompanied me on the inspection. Water and mud puddles were spread across the pad surface. As I assessed the well pad, I used an Oakton PCTS 50 and a Hanna Groline soil tester to field test various water/mud puddles. Most of the results were close to or below 1.0 mS. A location that in recent inspections tested at over 20.0 mS now measured 4.01 mS conductance. A water puddle on the east side of the pad measured 1.85 mS conductance. A 2'x6' water puddle on the fill slope above the south end of infiltration berm 1 field tested at 3.71 mS conductance.Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed on site by two retentive grading/infiltration areas. Infiltration area 2 does not meet the vegetative requirements yet. Both infiltration areas appeared to be functioning as designed with no visible evidence of accelerated erosion.The DEP recommends the following:1. Ensure crews follow procedures when removing the rig matting and plastic membrane to prevent contamination to the waters of the Commonwealth. 2. Immediately upon removal of secondary containment membrane, proceed with Act 2 remediation for areas with suspected contamination. 3. Intercept and capture the fluid with elevated conductance identified on the east fill slope as close to the source as possible to prevent the fluid from leaving the site and causing contamination to the waters of the Commonwealth.4. Continue to monitor the stability of infiltration area 2 and provide additional resources as necessary to achieve at least 70% uniform perennial vegetation.I left the site at 11:00 hrs.

Violation ID 780238

Unconventional Y

Comments Routine inspection conducted to assess overall site conditions during drilling operations. Ty Marine was the Chief company representative on site. I informed Mr. Marine of the area of sheen observed and recommended that the puddle be removed. Mr. Marine indicated that the puddle would be removed immediately. I revisited the site on March 08, 2017, with Kellon Balum of Chief. No sheen or odor was observed, indicating that the clean up efforts were effective. Title 25 Pa. Code Section 91.34(a) requires persons engaged in an activity which includes the impoundment, production, processing, transportation, storage, use, application or disposal of pollutants to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause. Since the observed release occurred off of containment, it was in violation of this requirement. However, since remedial measures were promptly taken and were effective, the violation is considered immediately corrected. All equipment operation on site should be regularly inspected for leaks and residual fluids that may be left during fueling and maintenance activities. Such measures would minimize the potential for releases occurring due to equipment leaks or poor housekeeping. Immediately corrected.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 976934
Permit API: 047-24180
Unconventional: No
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/29/2022
Comments: This inspection was performed following a report from DCNR that a hunter believed that there was a possible brine discharge from this location. The email was forwarded on 11/18/22, and it had been brought to the operator's attention on 11/17.It appears as though a brine leak has occurred sometime between DEP's 4/20/22 inspection and now. It is uncertain which tank the leak is emanating from, as the containment has been compromised and deer tracks are evident throughout.Some volume of brine has leached through the soil and come out on the east side of the containment on the edge of a swale. Significant deer activity has occurred at this point, causing rutting and erosion on the bank of the containment. Conductivity over 1 mS was noted with a meter at several points in the soil. The swale is currently running water, with slightly elevated conductivity noted in the water. As such, it is clear that brine discharge has occurred.The operator was contacted and stated that they would have someone visit the site on 11/30 to inspect, and would begin remediation after. Followup inspection will be done as necessary.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/31/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8158015
Permit API: 129-25727
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: East Huntingdon Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/31/2023
Comments: On August 31 2023, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the Adams 877-5 OG Well. The findings were as follows:The well site was located in an open field. The access road appeared stabilized at the time of this inspection. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection.At the time of this inspection, the well appeared equipped for production. The well tag was present at the time of this inspection. There were no observed leaks or discharge on the ground or around the wellhead. Upon inspection of the production tank there appeared to be a corroded valve near the base of the tank. Further inspection of this valve showed signs of apparent staining in the gravel, indicating a leak. Soil conductivity readings were taken under and near the valve and indicated elevated levels of contaminants with readings of 5.08mS, 4.86mS, and 2.79mS. Based on these observations, the Department recommends the operator assess the integrity of the production tank and corresponding production equipment, as well as assess the well site for leaks or spills and notify the Department of the findings within 10 days of receiving this inspection report. The Department is requesting the following information:1: What was released?2: When the release occurred?3: How long was the release occurring?4:Why the release occurred?5: The quantity of the release and how the quantity was determined?Based on today's inspection, violations 78.57 (a), 78.54, and SWMA 301 are being issued.

Comments: On February 4, 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Aphrodite Well Site (ESCGP issued on 5/9/2020, amended on 2/5/2024, expiring on 2/4/2029) in regards to a release reported to the Department on 2/3/2026 (CTS 394941). Present during the inspection was operator representative Jim Noon.According to Mr.Noon, this release is a seperate release, unrelated to the release documented in inspection report 4125373.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be installed in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) and site plans were present in the onsite mailbox. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel.At the time of inspection, there are 5 total wells on the well pad. According to the operator, stimulation for all 5 wells has been completed and they are continuing to install production equipment in order to get the wells into active production.During the inspection, Mr. Noon guided the Department to the location of the reported release. According to Mr. Noon the release was discovered on 2/3/2026 when containment for drilling/stimulation equipment was being removed from the site. He stated that upon removal of the containment, staining was observed and after further assessment it was identified as a release of impaired water and reported to the Department. At the time of the inspection the operator is unsure of the total volume of impaired water that was released.The Department observed the location of the spill and remediation. It appeared the area of the release and ongoing remediation was in an approximate 40-foot by 80-foot area adjacent to the well heads near the entrance of the well pad.Mr. Noon stated that 2 small temporary sumps were excavated in the area of the release in order to isolate the release. The water collected in the sumps were being pumped out by a vacuum truck. Mr. Noon stated that 2 roll-off boxes had already been filled with impacted material, and they were waiting for additional boxes to continue remediation.Conductivity readings of 18.08mS, and 6.13mS were obtained in the 2 excavated sumps. Conductivity readings of 3.97mS, 1.25mS, 1.17mS, and 0.69mS were obtained in the area of the release/remediation.The Department requests the operator provide a copy of the secondary containment inspection records from January 1, 2026, through the date the secondary containment was removed, within 3 days of receiving this inspection report.The operator is also requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.If the quantity of the spill is determined to be greater than 1 barrel (42 gallons),the operator will need to perform remediation in accordance with the Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2).Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued against the Aphrodite 2M well for the observed release. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending receipt and review of the requested information/documentation.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/15/2022 to PIN OAK ENERGY PARTNERS LLC in Jones Twp, Elk county. OGA3216(A) - WELL SITE RESTORATIONS - GENERAL RULE - Failure to restore disturbed land surface of a well site.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PIN OAK ENERGY PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/15/2022
Violation Code: OGA3216(A) - WELL SITE RESTORATIONS - GENERAL RULE - Failure to restore disturbed land surface of a well site.
Violation ID: 948147
Permit API: 047-24636
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/15/2022
Comments: This unconventional well is currently equipped for production and is equipped with a well tag displaying the well’s API number. The site ID sign at the entrance of the pad includes the required information, however it has become faded. Drilling operations were completed on this well on 10/13/2011. There is a second active well (047-24587) on this pad for which drilling operations were completed on 9/16/2011. Pin Oak has failed to restore this well site according to approved plans associated with ESX11-047-0024 and more than nine months have passed since the completion of drilling the last permitted well on this well site. Approximately one-half of this pad does not appear to be actively used for the operation of this well. There are four steel tanks labeled as holding production water located inside of a lined steel containment on this well site. At this time, the containment appears sound, as it is holding several inches of stormwater. A well development impoundment (Impoundment # 6) is located approximately 3800’ northeast of the HM2 well site (41.53798¿ / -78.70414¿). This impoundment is covered by the same ESCGP that encompasses the HM2 well site. The impoundment has not yet been restored, and greater than nine months have passed since the last well was serviced by this impoundment. The Department does not have record showing that this well development impoundment has been registered, as is required by Chapter 78a.59b(b). The access road leading to this well site and well development impoundment is in general holding up to current traffic levels. There are isolated areas of scouring that should be addressed in an effort to avoid potential E&S issues in the future. Routine maintenance/improvements to the road surface should be considered prior to any heavy equipment use of the road given its proximity to Bear Creek and several unnamed tributaries. Vegetative cover around the perimeter of the well site & well development impoundment, as well as the access road banks appears to be established. Future inspections will be conducted during the upcoming growing season to further evaluate the stabilization of earth disturbance associated with this well site & well development impoundment.

Inspection Date: 3/02/2021
Comments: This inspection report is written to document an incident response inspection conducted in response of a lube oil spill on the well site. Hilcorp Energy contacted the Department via telephone at approximately 9:50 AM on 3/2/21 to report a spill of lube oil close to the compressor on this McCullough well site. The volume lost was 175 gallons. I arrived on site at approximately 1:20 PM on 3/2/21. It appeared that somehow a leak developed from the elevated storage tank for the lube oil. This tank was located near the compressor unit for this well site. Most of the lube oil was cleaned up and material was placed in two drums on location. Very little oil was able to be seen on the ground surface, just staining. There were several 4" booms on the ground surface mostly surrounding the extent of the spill. The impacted area is roughly 15' x 25'. I called Brett Bunker and verified the details about the spill. He said a broken site tube on the tank was the cause of the spill. He said they will be back out tomorrow to start digging up the contaminated material (gravel and dirt). Laterally, the spill was contained. Vertically, Brett felt the oil would not travel much farther overnight. It was mentioned that because of the amount spilled, the clean-up would fall under the requirements of Chapter 78a.66 of the regulations. The contractor, S.E.T. Contracting from Lowellville Ohio, arrived while I was there and started unloading equipment for the clean-up.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection conducted a Follow-up inspection of the Seneca Resources - DCNR 007 Pad K located in Delmar Twp, Tioga Co. on 7/16/2019 @1300 hours. Activity onsite consisted of a front-end loader filling dump trucks with pad material that has been scraped up and stockpiled onsite. This material is being taken to DNCR 007 Pad D, to be used in the construction of the well pad. At the time of this inspection, the pad appears to have been scraped down, removing approximately 1.5' - 2' of pad material around the remaining secondary containment/rig mats. No puddles were observed onsite. Fluid in the gas buster secondary containment had a field measured conductivity of 4.23mS/cm. During a 5/21/19 inspection (IR#2885486) of the site, numerous puddles were discovered on the pad surface. Field screening indicated the conductivity ranged from 4 to >19.99 mS/cm. A sample was collected and upon the DEP receiving the results, they were communicated to Seneca and documented in an Administrative Inspection report (IR# 2897380) on 6/24/19. These results show elevated levels of chloride, strontium and barium indicating a release of a pollutional substance that exceeds Act 2 standards. This inspection report noted violations and requested information pertaining to the quantity of material released to the pad surface as well as what actions Seneca has done to remediate these releases. The NOV response received on 7/15/19 from Seneca failed to provide this information. Therefore, the violations cited will remain outstanding. Seneca should reference 78a66(c) to determine the actions necessary to achieve compliance at this location. I departed the site @1400 hours.
